comment: The wheel parity check's table (tools/bindings/wheelparity.py): for a QuantLib-Python name the bindings make no type of, a route names what a user reaches instead and why, its kind saying what the check verifies: a type the surface makes, an enum it carries, a C function it has, or a language form in prose; an exclusion pattern names a ruled exclusion; a note records a residual difference a crossing class keeps.

Array.why: QuantLib's Array is an array in each layer

Matrix.why: a working type crossing as its values

Average.why: a SWIG enum holder: the enum

Parameter.why: the abstract base: its concrete parameters (ConstantParameter, NullParameter, PiecewiseConstantParameter)

ForwardEuropeanEngine.why: QuantLib's ForwardVanillaEngine<AnalyticEuropeanEngine>: the engine bound to an analytic European engine

exclusions..*Handle: a handle (R1: no handles; objects are values)
exclusions.SimpleQuote: a quote (R1: quotes are values, doubles)
exclusions..*Vector|.*VectorVector|.*Pair|.*PairVec: a SWIG container: a list, tuple or map in each layer (BIR5, BIR11, BIR21)
exclusions.(DMinus|DPlus|DPlusDMinus|DZero|Dirichle: a stepping part, or a member taking one (BIR3's (A))
exclusions.(CompositeQuote|DerivedQuote|MultiCompos: takes the caller's own function (BIR11 as amended: out of 2.0)

notes.GlobalBootstrap: QuantLib-Python's constructor takes an initial guess as a list of values; nanoql's is initialGuessFn, a delegate the C ABI leaves at its default, so a binding can't pass one (the bindings' drop rule).
